title: The Slow Ionized Wind and Rotating Disklike System that are Associated with the High-mass Young Stellar Object G345.4938+01.4677
question: Is the ionized gas around the high-mass YSO G345.49+1.47 a slow photo-ionized wind rather than a fast jet, as probed by 3 mm continuum and hydrogen recombination lines, and do sulfur-bearing molecules trace a rotating disklike core?

data.sensitivity: continuum ~50 uJy/beam; lines 1-2 mJy/beam per channel

what.value: Centimeter continuum jet/lobe fluxes and spectral index below 10 GHz (0.85+-0.15), inclination ~45 deg, momentum rate

evidence.quote: The inclination angle $i$ was estimated as $\sim45$$^\circ$ by (cite: Guzman2010ApJ), based on the appearance of the 2 $\mu$m image of the inner cavity
we adopt a distance to IRAS 16562$-$3959 of 1.7 kpc (cite: Lopez2011AA).

what.value: Line frequencies and Eu from JPL and CDMS via Splatalogue

evidence.quote: obtained from the JPL (cite: Pickett1998JQSRT) and CDMS (cite: Muller2001AA) databases consulted through the Splatalogue

recipe.goal: Recalibrate and image continuum and cubes
recipe.method: CASA recalibration, phase self-cal, clean with robust 0, uvcontsub

recipe.goal: Measure continuum sources and spectral indices
recipe.method: maxfit peak positions, imfit 2D Gaussians for sources 10 and 13, box-integrated fluxes, weighted least-squares spectral index
key_parameters: detection threshold 0.75 mJy; boxes of two times beam size; flux uncertainty 2 sigma ~0.1 mJy

recipe.goal: Fit Voigt profiles to HRLs and derive electron density
recipe.method: Joint chi2 minimization of Voigt functions over three HRLs between -80 and 100 km/s with shared T; Gaussian width 0.22 sqrt(T); Ne from Griem/Walmsley relation
key_parameters: sigma = 1 mJy per channel; T fixed at 7000 K after fit

recipe.goal: Model continuum and HRLs with ionized wind model
recipe.method: Reynolds-type isothermal power-law jet model; LTE line flux from integral over continuum opacity
key_parameters: i=45 deg, r0=100 AU, S100GHz=120.6 mJy, alpha_op=0.92, T0=7000 K; conical eps=1, theta0=0.33, Ne0=2.19e7 cm-3
assumptions: Hydrogen only, constant ionization fraction, isothermal, negligible bulk motions

recipe.method: Boltzmann diagram with optically thin single excitation temperature models, two-component fit for SO2 and 34SO; opacity from 32SO/34SO ratios
key_parameters: line fluxes within 5"x5" box, V -30 to 0 km/s; uncertainty 15 mJy km/s
assumptions: d=1.7 kpc; [32S/34S]=22.5; rate coefficient 1e-11 cm3/s for high-energy SO2

recipe.method: PV diagram of SO2 8(3,5)-9(2,8) perpendicular to jet; 50% contour size and velocity breadth in simplified Franco-Hernandez formula

evidence.loc: 4.2 The ionized jet observed at 92 GHz
evidence.quote: power law in frequency with an spectral index of $0.92\pm0.01$ over the entire frequency range

answer_key.quantity: Dust flux of Source 10 at 92 GHz

evidence.loc: 4.2 The ionized jet observed at 92 GHz
evidence.quote: we find that the flux attributable to dust is $\sim11$ mJy at 92 GHz, that is, $\sim$10% of the total flux
We find a characteristic value for the electron density of $5\times10^7$ cm$^{-3}$.
Our best-fit model indicates that this temperature is $T=2000^{+6000}_{-1000}$ K.
with temperatures of $140^{+60}_{-20}$ and $35^{+25}_{-20}$ K, respectively
we derive a dynamical mass of $56\mbox{$\,M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$}$.
